header.userPrompt:
Refactor the bank-statement review page (`/bank-statements/:id`) to hold its data in page-scoped reactive Vars instead of re-fetching and remounting. Frontend only: no backend, API, model, endpoint, or database changes. Behavior must stay identical; this is purely how the page owns and refreshes its state.

## The problem being fixed
The page loads its data through `AsyncComponent` in `BankStatementReviewPage.scala` and renders `BankStatementReviewContent`, which seeds local `useState` from the `data` prop. The parent remounts the content (via `.withKey(timesRefreshing)`) on every refresh to reseed that state, and several actions trigger a full re-fetch of all endpoints, which swaps the whole body for the loading spinner (a visible flicker):
- "Process ready" (bulk) calls `onRefresh -> forceRefresh()`, re-fetching everything and remounting.
- Creating an expense/refund/rule calls `showToast(...)` (page-level state), which re-renders the page and makes `AsyncComponent` re-fetch.
- Switching tabs calls `history.replace(...?tab=...)`, a router re-render that again re-fetches.
Single-row link/ignore already update local state in place and do NOT remount, that is the behavior we want everywhere.

## Target design
Use the project's existing reactive primitive: `monix.reactive.subjects.Var[T]` read with `net.wiringbits.core.ReactiveHooks.useValue` (the same mechanism as `AppContext.$auth`). Use `useValue`, not `useDistinctValue` (these values change only on an explicit load/patch, so no `cats.Eq` is needed).

Hold the review page's data in page-scoped Vars, created ONCE per statement id (stable across renders via `useRef`/`useMemo` keyed on the statement id, never a fresh `Var` per render, which would churn the `useValue` subscription) and re-created when the id changes. Suggested boundaries (use judgment, but keep these concerns separate so each re-renders only its own consumers):
- the statement metadata for the header (bank, period, account label, status) — this never changes after load, so it can be an immutable loaded value rather than a Var;
- a Var for the statement rows (`List[GetBankStatement.StatementRowData]`) — the table; mutated by every row action;
- a Var for the support data: merchants, categories, import rules, and the unlinked-expense list used for reconciliation;
- a Var for the AI suggestions (`Option[AiSuggestions]`), polled independently.

Two fetch stages, each a one-shot that writes its Var(s), NOT a per-render fetch:
1. `getBankStatement(id)` — returns metadata, rows, and `aiSuggestions` in one call. Seed the metadata, the rows Var, and the suggestions Var from it. The header renders as soon as this lands.
2. The support endpoints (`getMerchants`, `getCategories`, `getImportRules`, `getExpensesFiltered` over the candidate window) — seed the support Var. The table shows rows from stage 1 immediately and enriches (merchant/category names, rule resolution, expense matching) when stage 2 arrives.

You may keep `AsyncComponent` purely for the initial per-stage loading UI, or model loading as a small ADT in a Var; either way it must fetch only on mount / when the statement id changes, and must never re-fetch because of an incidental re-render. Do not key `AsyncComponent` on the fetched data, and remove the `timesRefreshing`/`forceRefresh` full-reload and the content remount-to-reseed entirely.

## Mutations patch the Vars in place (no reload, no remount)
Every action updates the relevant Var directly, the way single-row actions already update local state:
- single-row link / ignore / unlink / unlink-refund / unignore -> patch the rows Var (and refresh the expense list in the support Var where the current code calls `refreshExpenses`);
- drawer create expense / create refund / link expense / create rule -> patch the rows Var (set `expenseId`/`refundId`), and for rule/merchant creation append to the support Var; keep the existing toast;
- bulk "Process ready" and "Ignore" -> patch the affected rows in the rows Var as each completes (set `expenseId`/`refundId`/`ignoredAt`), instead of `forceRefresh()`. A bulk-created expense returns only its id; set that id so the row leaves the Ready filter (as single-row create already does via `refreshRow`), re-reading the row for its merchant/category is acceptable but must not reload the page.
Tabs stay pure projections over the rows Var via `BankStatementReviewLogic.filterRows`; switching tabs must not fetch. Keep the `?tab=` URL sync if it can be done without triggering a data re-fetch; if it can't cleanly, prefer correct behavior (no flicker) over the URL param.

## AI suggestions
Put suggestions in their own Var, seeded from the stage-1 response. Keep the existing polling (`BankStatementSuggestionsPolling`) and regenerate behavior, but the poll must update ONLY the suggestions Var, never the rows or metadata, so a poll tick never disturbs the table. (The poll may continue to call `getBankStatement` and read just `aiSuggestions` from the response; a dedicated lighter endpoint is out of scope.) Preserve the existing per-row "pending" indicator.

## Keep identical
All current behavior: the five tabs with their counts, the name filter, the drawer forms, the bulk bar + results + toast, reconciliation matching, primary actions, suggestion polling/regeneration, and the route and navigation entry points. `BankStatementReviewLogic` stays pure; keep and extend its tests. Do not change reconciliation logic, the reviewers, or any server code.

## Out of scope
No backend/API/endpoint/model/DB changes. No new suggestions endpoint. No page-level suggestion status banner (separate task). No change to the statements list page.

## Tests
Keep `BankStatementReviewLogic` pure and its specs green; add coverage for any new pure helper. Follow `docs/guide/testing.md`. The full suite must pass as CI runs it.

resultJson.description:
The bank-statement review page (`/bank-statements/:stmtId`) currently loads everything through one `AsyncComponent` fetch in `BankStatementReviewPage`, then renders `BankStatementReviewContent`, which copies the loaded `ReviewData` into local `useState`. To pick up changes, the page bumps a `useForceRefresh` counter. That re-fetches all five endpoints and remounts the content via `.withKey(timesRefreshing)`, so the whole body flickers to the spinner. Bulk "Process ready" ends with `onRefresh()`, and toasts and tab switches cause incidental re-renders that also re-fetch. Only single-row link and ignore behave the way we want: they patch local state in place.

This epic moves the page's data into page-scoped monix `Var`s held in a small store object. The store is created once per statement id and read with `ReactiveHooks.useValue`. Loading happens in two one-shot stages, and both fire only when the statement id changes. Stage 1 is `getBankStatement`, which seeds the immutable statement metadata for the header, the rows Var and the AI-suggestions Var. Stage 2 is merchants, categories, import rules and unlinked expenses, which seed the support Var. The table shows stage-1 rows straight away and fills in names, rule matches and expense matches when stage 2 lands. Every mutation patches the relevant Var directly: single-row actions, drawer create/link/rule, bulk ignore and bulk process. The suggestion poll writes only the suggestions Var. The `timesRefreshing`/`forceRefresh` reload and the remount-to-reseed are removed.

This is frontend only (`web/`). There are no backend, API, model, endpoint or DB changes. User-visible behavior stays the same apart from the missing flicker: five tabs with counts, `?tab=` URL sync, name filter, drawer forms, bulk bar, results and toast, reconciliation matching, primary actions, polling and regeneration with the per-row pending indicator, and the existing route and nav entry points. `BankStatementReviewLogic` stays pure; its specs and the bulk-run specs stay green and get extended.

tasks.title: Add a pure load-state ADT, support/row patch helpers and the page-scoped review store
Make single-row and bulk actions take updater functions instead of React setters
tasks.description:
Refactor `BankStatementRowActions.scala` and `BankStatementBulkRuns.scala` so they no longer depend on `SetStateHookCallback` for the data they patch. Make the following parameters plain functions:
- `setStatementRows` becomes `updateRows: (List[GetBankStatement.StatementRowData] => List[GetBankStatement.StatementRowData]) => Unit`;
- `setExpenseList` becomes `setExpenses: List[GetExpenses.Response.Expense] => Unit`.

Use the new `patchRow`/`replaceRow` helpers from Logic where they simplify the code.

In `handleBulkImport`, rename `onRefresh` to `onFinished: () => Unit`. Its call stays at the same place, after the toast. Keep the selection and BulkRun setters as they are; they are UI state.

In `BankStatementReviewContent`, adapt the call sites to pass `f => setStatementRows(cur => f(cur))` and `setExpenseList(_)`, and keep passing `props.onRefresh` as `onFinished` for now. Page behavior is unchanged in this task.

Update `BankStatementBulkRunsSpec`: give the `Recorder` an updater-function form and rename the "refresh once" test to describe `onFinished`. Follow RULE-TE-001 and don't put the type name in descriptions.

Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementBulkRunsSpec"`.

tasks.title: Decouple suggestions polling from the whole statement
tasks.description:
Change `BankStatementSuggestionsPolling.useSuggestionsPolling` to take `stmtId: UUID`, `aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions]` and `setAiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions] => Unit`, replacing `statement` and `setStatement`.

- Poll tick: `client.getBankStatement(stmtId)` and then `setAiSuggestions(full.aiSuggestions)` only.
- Regenerate success: `setAiSuggestions(Some(resp.aiSuggestions))`.
- Keep the attempts cap, the interval, the `suggestionsPollKey` effect key, `regenerateDisabled`, the toast and the error handling exactly as they are.

In `BankStatementReviewContent`, call it with `statement.id`, `statement.aiSuggestions` and `s => setStatement(cur => cur.copy(aiSuggestions = s))`, so behavior is unchanged in this task.

If you pull any pure piece out of the hook (for example the polling/disabled predicates), test it in `BankStatementReviewLogicSpec`. Otherwise, `CI=true sbt Test/compile` plus `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReviewLogicSpec"` is enough.

tasks.title: Move the review page onto the store: two-stage one-shot load, in-place patches, no forceRefresh/remount
tasks.description:
Rewire `BankStatementReviewPage.scala` and `BankStatementReviewContent.scala` onto `BankStatementReviewStore`.

Page:
- Keep the stmtId parsing, the toast and the bulk-run states, and update the 'survive the remount' comment.
- Render `BankStatementReviewContent(ctx, stmtId, showToast, bulk…)` with `.withKey(stmtId.toString)`. This is statement identity, not a refresh counter.
- Remove `GenericHooks.useForceRefresh`, `AsyncComponent`, `fetch`, `ReviewData` usage and `onRefresh`. Also remove the `ReviewData` case class from Logic, and any imports your change leaves unused.

Content:
- `val store = SafeHooks.useMemo(stmtId.toString)(() => new BankStatementReviewStore()(using Scheduler.global))`.
- `SafeHooks.useEffect(stmtId.toString)`: stage 1 `getBankStatement(stmtId)` leads to `store.statementLoaded`, or to `statementFailed` on failure. Then stage 2 runs merchants, categories, rules (`ImportRuleMatcher.Rule.fromApi`) and `getExpensesFiltered(candidateExpenseWindow(stmt), unlinkedOnly = true)`, leading to `store.supportLoaded(ReviewSupport(...))` or `supportFailed`.
- Read state with `ReactiveHooks.useValue(store.$statement / $rows / $support / $suggestions)`.
- Render states:
  - statement Loading: `Loader(props.ctx)`;
  - statement Failed: the message in the existing error-typography style;
  - statement Loaded: header, tabs and table built from the rows.
- While support is not Loaded, compute rowInfo with empty lists.
- Gate actions on support until it is Loaded:
  - disable bulk Process/Ignore (`bulkActive`). Otherwise a ready-by-AI row could be bulk-created with no expense matching, which would make duplicate expenses;
  - do not render the drawer forms; render nothing or a Loader in their place.
- Show `supportFailed` in the existing error slot.
- Memo keys stay `toString` keys derived from the Var values.

Wiring:
- Build `BankStatementRowActions` with `updateRows = store.updateRows`, `setExpenses = es => store.updateSupport(_.withExpenses(es))` and `expenseWindow` from the loaded statement.
- Drawer callbacks use `store.patchRow` for `expenseId`/`refundId` plus `rowActions.refreshRow` where it is called today. `onRuleCreated`/`onNewEntities` use `store.updateSupport(_.withRule / _.withMerchant)`. Keep the toasts.
- Bulk import: `onFinished = () => rowActions.refreshExpenses()` replaces the full reload. Rows are already patched per row. Bulk ignore uses `store.updateRows`.
- Polling uses `store.$suggestions` value and `store.setSuggestions`.
- Tabs stay `filterRows` projections. Keep `handleTabChange`'s `history.replace(?tab=)`: with fetches keyed only on stmtId it no longer re-fetches.
- Delete the unused `rowEdits` state: its seed (`props.data`) no longer exists.

Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and `sbt "web/testOnly *BankStatementReview* *BankStatementBulkRunsSpec"`. Optionally sanity-check in the running app that Process ready, drawer create, rule create and tab switch show no spinner and make no repeated getMerchants/getCategories calls.

resultJson.brief:
## Modules
- `web/` holds the Scala.js + Slinky 0.7 + React 18 + MUI 5 frontend. It is the only module touched. `lib/api/shared/` holds the shared Tapir models and `ApiClient`: read it, don't change it. Never touch `server/`.
- All review-page files are in `web/src/main/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`. Specs are in `web/src/test/scala/net/wiringbits/components/pages/`.

## Files
- `BankStatementReviewPage.scala` is the route component (`AppRouter.scala:95`, `/bank-statements/:stmtId`). It parses `stmtId` with `useParams` and holds the page-level `toast` (Snackbar + `dom.window.setTimeout` clear), `bulkIgnore` and `bulkImport: BulkRun` state. Today it uses `GenericHooks.useForceRefresh` + `AsyncComponent[ReviewData](fetch, render, progressIndicator = () => Loader(ctx), watchedObjects = List(timesRefreshing))` and remounts the content with `.withKey(timesRefreshing.toString)`. The stage-2 fetch already exists there: expenses come from `client.getExpensesFiltered(Some(from), Some(to), unlinkedOnly = true)` with `(from, to) = BankStatementReviewLogic.candidateExpenseWindow(statement)`. Rules map via `ImportRuleMatcher.Rule.fromApi`. Merchants, categories and rules responses are `.data`.
- `BankStatementReviewContent.scala` is the page body. It holds local `useState` for:
  - `statement`, `statementRows`, `rowEdits` (unused), `error`;
  - merchant, category, rule and expense lists;
  - `rowFilter` (initial value from `?tab=`, default "ready"), `selectedRowIds`, `drawerState`.

  It derives `effectiveRuleList` (`ImportRuleMatcher.effectiveRules(ruleList, merchants.map(m => m.id -> m.name))`), `rowInfoById`, `unlinkedExpensesByDate` (`ReconciliationMatcher.unlinkedByDate`) and `expenseMatchById` via `SafeHooks.useMemo` with `toString` keys. `onRowAction`/`onToggleSelected` are `SafeHooks.useCallback` with stable deps, so they may only capture stable things; a store built once per stmtId is ideal. `handleTabChange` calls `history.replace(s"$pathname?tab=$tab")`. It renders Header, Tabs, BulkBar, the error line, Table, BulkResults and Drawer.
- `BankStatementRowActions.scala` is a case class with `ignore`, `unignore`, `unlink` (calls `refreshExpenses`), `unlinkRefund`, `refreshRow(rowId)` and `refreshExpenses()`. `refreshRow` re-reads `getBankStatement` and replaces one row, then refreshes expenses. Today it takes `SetStateHookCallback`s.
- `BankStatementBulkRuns.scala` has `handleBulkIgnore` and `handleBulkImport`. Each runs a sequential loop over ids, and each row's decision comes from `bulkRowDecision`. They already patch rows per success: set `ignoredAt`, `expenseId` + `expenseMerchantId`/`expenseCategoryId`, or `refundId`. The only full reload is `onRefresh()` at the end of import.
- `BankStatementSuggestionsPolling.scala` provides the hook `useSuggestionsPolling(client, statement, setStatement, setError, showToast)`, which returns `State(polling, regenerateDisabled, regenerate)`. It polls every 3000 ms, at most 20 attempts, while `suggestionsPending(ai)`. Its effect key is `s"$stmtId:$pollingSuggestions"`.
- `BankStatementReviewHeader.scala` reads only the metadata fields of `GetBankStatement.Response` (id, documentFilename, bankName, productType, currency, accountLast4, periodStart/End), plus `rowCount` and the regenerate props. Passing the stage-1 response unchanged is fine.
- `BankStatementReviewDrawer.scala` Props: ctx, stmtId, `target: Option[(Row, DrawerState)]`, merchants, categories, ruleList, aiSuggestions, onClose, onCancel, `onExpenseCreated(rowId, expenseId)`, `onRefundCreated`, `onExpenseLinked`, `onRuleCreated(rowId, rule, Option[Merchant])`, `onNewEntities(Option[Rule], Option[Merchant])`.
- `BankStatementReviewLogic.scala` is pure (no React or MUI). It has `ReviewData` (to be removed once unused), `candidateExpenseWindow`, `suggestionsPending`, `canRegenerateSuggestions`, `rowInfo`, `expenseMatches`, `filterRows(rows, tab, rowInfoById)`, `bulkRowDecision`, `bulkImportSummary`, `BulkRun`, `DrawerState` and `RowInfo`.
- Model `GetBankStatement.Response` lives in `lib/api/shared/.../models/bankstatements/GetBankStatement.scala`. It has `statementRows: List[StatementRowData]` and `aiSuggestions: Option[AiSuggestions]`. `StatementRowData` fields: id, index, date, amount, description, manuallyEdited, confirmedAt, expenseId, refundId, ignoredAt, txnType, expenseMerchantId, expenseCategoryId.

## Reactive primitive
- `net.wiringbits.core.ReactiveHooks.useValue[T](v: Var[T]): T` is `useState(v())` plus an effect that subscribes `v.foreach(setState)`, keyed on the Var reference. The Var must therefore be stable across renders: create it in `SafeHooks.useMemo(stmtId.toString)`, never inline. A monix `Var` replays its current value on subscribe, so nothing is lost between first render and subscription.
- `monix.reactive.subjects.Var[T](initial)(using scheduler)`. Read with `v()`, write with `v := x`. Production uses `monix.execution.Scheduler.global` (see `Main.scala`, `ReactiveHooks`). Tests use `Scheduler.trampoline()` (allowed only in tests, per testing.md).
- `AsyncComponent` (slinky-utils 0.7.2, no sources locally) re-runs its fetch whenever `watchedObjects` changes and is not designed for staged loading. The plan replaces it with a `Loadable` ADT in a Var, fetched in `SafeHooks.useEffect(stmtId.toString)`. Keying the content on `stmtId` gives each statement a fresh store, so stale futures from a previous id write to an orphaned store, which is harmless.

## Conventions
- Hook deps: always `SafeHooks.useEffect/useMemo/useCallback` with `String` keys (RULE-FE-006). `Hooks.*` is used directly only in `net.wiringbits.core`.
- Handle API results with `.onComplete { case Success / Failure(ex) => setError(ex.getMessage) }` (RULE-FE-008).
- No `js.Dynamic` or `asInstanceOf` in pages (RULE-FE-014). Use `.fold[ReactElement](Fragment())` for optional elements. No object-level `val` React elements.
- No hacks or `setTimeout` ordering tricks. Don't silently default missing data. Match the existing comment density and naming. Remove imports/vals your change orphans. Don't refactor unrelated code.
- Tests: ScalaTest `AnyWordSpec` + `must` matchers. `should`/`in` descriptions describe behavior and never repeat the class or object name (RULE-TE-001, enforced since #71). Prefer pure-function tests over DOM tests (RULE-TE-010). `BankStatementBulkRunsSpec` shows the pattern: a `StubClient extends ApiClient(...)(using ExecutionContext.parasitic, SttpBackendStub.asynchronousFuture)`, a `Recorder` for setters, and `ExecutionContext.parasitic` to run loops synchronously.
- Build: `CI=true` makes warnings errors. Verify with `CI=true sbt Test/compile` and targeted `sbt "web/testOnly *XSpec"`. Do NOT run the full `sbt test`. Web tests need Node 24 on PATH; the default shell node is v16, which makes yarn install fail.
- Formatting: `sbt scalafmtAll scalafmtSbt` before committing.
